items.prompt: Which sentence uses brackets correctly?

options.text: Lake Toba (in North Sumatra is) the largest lake in Indonesia.
options.why: Is belongs to the main sentence, so it should be outside the brackets.

options.text: Lake Toba (in North Sumatra) is the largest lake in Indonesia.
(Lake Toba) in North Sumatra is the largest lake in Indonesia.
options.why: Lake Toba is the subject of the sentence, so it should not be in brackets.

options.text: Lake Toba in (North Sumatra is the largest lake) in Indonesia.
options.why: The brackets hold part of the main sentence.

hints: Brackets hold extra information.
Read each sentence without the words in brackets. It should still make sense.
Which words tell you extra information about where Lake Toba is?
items.explanation: In North Sumatra is extra information, so it goes in brackets. Lake Toba is the largest lake in Indonesia makes sense without it.

items.prompt: Which phrase needs hyphens?

options.why: Small describes the girl on its own, so no hyphen is needed.
Happy describes the girl on its own.
Ten comes after the noun here, so no hyphens are needed.

hints: Hyphens join words that work together to describe a noun.
Look for a group of words before the noun that act as one describing word.
Ask: do ten, year and old describe the girl together?
items.explanation: Ten, year and old work together to describe the girl, so they are joined with hyphens: a ten-year-old girl.

items.prompt: Two words should be joined with a hyphen. Write them with the hyphen. My sister is a well known singer.
hints: Look at the words just before singer.
Two words that describe a noun together are often joined with a hyphen.
Find the two words that tell us what kind of singer she is.
items.explanation: Well and known work together to describe singer, so they are joined: a well-known singer.

items.prompt: Which punctuation could replace the brackets? Our teacher (Mr Halim) loves astronomy.

options.why: Full stops would break the sentence into pieces.
Colons introduce lists or explanations.
Question marks end questions.

hints: Brackets mark extra information.
Another pair of punctuation marks can also mark extra information.
Try reading the sentence with a short pause before and after Mr Halim.
items.explanation: A pair of commas can also mark extra information: Our teacher, Mr Halim, loves astronomy.

items.prompt: Which sentence uses commas correctly to add extra information?

options.text: Pak Joko the school, gardener grows orchids.
options.why: The commas should go around the school gardener.

options.text: Pak Joko, the school gardener grows orchids.
options.why: The extra information needs a comma at the end too.

options.text: Pak Joko, the school gardener, grows orchids.
Pak, Joko the school gardener, grows orchids.
options.why: The first comma should come after Joko, not after Pak.

hints: Find the extra information about Pak Joko.
Extra information needs a comma before it and a comma after it.
Read the sentence without the school gardener. Does it still make sense?
items.explanation: The school gardener is extra information about Pak Joko, so it has a comma on each side.

items.prompt: Which sentence means that the chair will be given a new cover?

options.text: We will recover the old chair.
options.why: Recover means get something back or get better after an illness.

options.text: We will discover the old chair.
options.why: Discover means find.

options.text: We will uncover the old chair.
options.why: Uncover means take a cover off.

options.text: We will re-cover the old chair.

hints: The hyphen changes how the word is read.
Re- means again, so re-cover means cover again.
Replace the long word in each sentence with its meaning. Which one is about a new cover?
items.explanation: Re-cover with a hyphen means cover again. Without the hyphen, recover means get better or get something back.

items.prompt: Sort the phrases: does it need a hyphen or not?
hints: Hyphens join words that work together as one describing word or one name.
If the describing words come before the noun, they often need a hyphen.
Start with a fast moving river. Do fast and moving work together to describe the river?
items.explanation: A fast-moving river, a sugar-free drink and my mother-in-law need hyphens. In the other phrases, the words come after the noun or work separately.

items.prompt: Add brackets. Write the words that should go inside them. The Komodo dragon the largest lizard in the world can be found in Indonesia.

answers: the largest lizard in the world

hints: Brackets hold extra information that the sentence could manage without.
Find the words that describe the Komodo dragon.
Read the sentence without those words. Does it still make sense?
items.explanation: The largest lizard in the world is extra information about the Komodo dragon, so it goes in brackets.

items.prompt: Choose all the sentences that are punctuated correctly.

options.text: The concert (which started late) was wonderful.
My brother, a keen cyclist, rode 40 kilometres.

options.why: Was belongs to the main sentence and should not be in brackets.

options.text: We saw a twelve-metre-long whale shark.
A sugar, free drink is healthier.
options.why: Sugar-free needs a hyphen, not a comma.

hints: Check each pair of brackets, each pair of commas and each hyphen.
Extra information must be removable. Hyphens join words that describe a noun together.
Read each sentence without the bracketed or comma-marked words. Does it still work?
items.explanation: The correct sentences mark extra information with brackets or a pair of commas, and twelve-metre-long uses hyphens to describe the whale shark.

items.prompt: Which sentence means that about thirty people came to the party?

options.text: Thirty-odd people came to the party.
Thirty odd people came to the party.
options.why: Without a hyphen, odd describes the people, so it means thirty strange people!

options.text: Thirty, odd people came to the party.
options.why: The comma makes this confusing and does not mean about thirty.

options.text: Thirty (odd) people came to the party.
options.why: The brackets make odd extra information about the people.

hints: Odd can mean strange, but it can also mean roughly or a few more than.
A hyphen joins a number to odd when it means roughly that number.
Look for the sentence where thirty and odd are joined.
items.explanation: Thirty-odd means about thirty. Without the hyphen, thirty odd people means thirty strange people.

items.prompt: Which sentence uses commas in a list correctly?
hints: A comma separates items in a list.
The last two items are joined with and, not a comma.
Check for a missing comma after apples.
items.explanation: Use commas between items in a list. The last item is usually joined by and.

options.text: We bought apples bananas, grapes and oranges.
options.why: A comma is missing after apples.

options.text: We bought apples, bananas, grapes and oranges.
We bought, apples, bananas, grapes and oranges.
options.why: There is no need for a comma after bought.

options.text: We bought apples, bananas, grapes, and, oranges.
options.why: There is no comma needed after and.

items.prompt: Which marks can show extra information in a sentence?
hints: Extra information often goes in the middle of a sentence.
It is put inside a pair of marks.
The marks look like curved lines.
items.explanation: Brackets, commas or dashes can show extra information. Brackets are a pair of curved marks.

options.why: Question marks end questions. They do not show extra information.
Capital letters start sentences and names. They do not show extra information.
These show strong feeling. They do not hold extra information.

items.prompt: Put the cards in order to make a sentence with brackets.
hints: The extra information goes in brackets.
The bracket opens before a and closes after terrier.
Start with My dog.
items.explanation: The extra information a small terrier is placed in brackets after the noun it describes.
items.answer: My dog (a small terrier) loves bones.

items.prompt: Which phrase means a shark that attacks people?
hints: A hyphen joins words so they work as one describing word.
Which words describe the shark together?
Man and eating describe the shark together.
items.explanation: Man-eating is a describing word made from two words. The hyphen shows that it belongs to the shark.

options.why: Without the hyphen it could mean a man who is eating shark.
The hyphen is in the wrong place.
Only man and eating should be joined. Shark is a separate word.

items.prompt: Join two words with a hyphen. Write the phrase. She is a hard working nurse.
hints: The two words join to describe the nurse.
A hyphen joins them into one describing word.
Hard comes first.
items.explanation: Hard-working is a compound describing word before a noun. The hyphen joins the two words.

items.prompt: Mr Hadi ___ our caretaker ___ is retiring.
hints: Extra information about Mr Hadi is in the middle.
Commas can go either side of extra information.
The same mark is used on both sides.
items.explanation: A pair of commas can mark off extra information in a sentence.

items.prompt: Which sentence uses brackets correctly?
hints: Brackets surround only the extra information.
The sentence still makes sense if you remove the brackets and what is inside.
Remove the brackets and the words inside. What remains?
items.explanation: The sentence works without the words in brackets, so they are extra information.

options.text: The orangutan (found in Borneo and Sumatra) is a red-haired ape.
The orangutan (found in Borneo and Sumatra, is a red-haired ape).
options.why: The closing bracket is in the wrong place. The extra information ends after Sumatra.

options.text: The orangutan found (in Borneo and Sumatra) is a red-haired ape.
options.why: The brackets do not hold the whole extra phrase.

options.text: (The orangutan found in Borneo and Sumatra) is a red-haired ape.
options.why: The brackets are around the main part of the sentence instead of the extra part.

items.prompt: Match each phrase to its meaning.
hints: The hyphen shows that re means again.
Without the hyphen the word has a new meaning.
Start with recover from a cold.
items.explanation: A hyphen can show that re means again. Without it, the word may mean something else.
pairs: put a new cover on it
change it to make it better

items.prompt: Which words should go inside brackets? Write them. The festival was held in Yogyakarta a city in Java last month.
hints: Look for the extra information about Yogyakarta.
It gives more detail about a place.
It starts with a.
items.explanation: A city in Java is extra information about Yogyakarta, so it goes inside brackets.

items.prompt: Which sentence has commas that mark off extra information correctly?
hints: Extra information needs a comma on both sides.
Cover the words who lives in Surabaya. Is the sentence still complete?
Look for two commas around who lives in Surabaya.
items.explanation: A pair of commas marks off extra information, one before and one after.

options.text: My brother who lives in Surabaya, is a chef.
options.why: There is a comma after Surabaya but not before who.

options.text: My brother, who lives in Surabaya, is a chef.
My brother, who lives, in Surabaya is a chef.
options.why: The commas are in the wrong places. They should surround the extra information.

options.text: My brother, who lives in Surabaya is a chef.
options.why: The second comma is missing after Surabaya.

items.prompt: Join the describing words with hyphens.
hints: Hyphens join words that work together before a noun.
Write the whole phrase again with hyphens.
The words well and behaved belong together.
items.explanation: When words join to describe a noun, they are often linked with hyphens: well-behaved, two-storey, out-of-date.
head: Before
After

items.prompt: Put the cards in order to make a correct sentence.
hints: The extra information is set off with commas.
A talented dancer tells us more about her cousin.
Start with Her cousin.
items.explanation: A talented dancer is extra information about her cousin. A pair of commas surrounds it.
items.answer: Her cousin, a talented dancer, won first prize.

items.prompt: Which phrase means twenty bottles, each holding five litres?
hints: Work out which words belong together as a size.
Five-litre describes each bottle.
Twenty is how many.
items.explanation: Five-litre is a describing word for the bottles. Twenty is the number of bottles.

options.why: This could mean twenty-five bottles of one litre each.
Without hyphens we cannot tell how many bottles or how big.
This means bottles that each hold twenty-five litres.

items.prompt: Choose all the phrases with hyphens used correctly.
hints: Hyphens join words that work as a describing word before a noun.
In a hyphenated phrase before a noun, the middle words are usually singular.
Adverbs ending in -ly are not joined with a hyphen.
items.explanation: Well-known, five-year-old and up-to-date are correct. Adverbs ending in -ly do not take a hyphen.

options.why: Years should be singular when it comes before a noun in a hyphenated phrase.
Adverbs ending in -ly do not need a hyphen.
The hyphen is in the wrong place. Well and known belong together.

items.prompt: Which sentence means that only some of the pupils missed the bus?
hints: Think about whether the information is essential or just extra.
Without commas, the words who were late tell us which pupils.
With commas, they are extra information about all pupils.
items.explanation: Without commas, who were late identifies which pupils. With commas it is extra information about all of them.

options.text: The pupils, who were late, missed the bus.
options.why: The commas make who were late extra information, so all the pupils were late.

options.text: The pupils who were late missed the bus.
The pupils (who were late) missed the bus.
options.why: The brackets also make it extra information, so all the pupils were late.

options.text: The pupils, who were late missed the bus.
options.why: The comma makes it unclear. It suggests all the pupils were late.

items.prompt: Which phrase means twenty children who are each four years old?
hints: Four-year-old is the age of each child.
Twenty is how many children there are.
Where do the hyphens need to go?
items.explanation: Four-year-old is a describing word and twenty is the number of children.

options.why: This suggests twenty-four children who are each one year old.
This means children who are each twenty-four years old.
Without hyphens the meaning is not clear at all.

items.prompt: True or false: A hyphen can join words to make a compound adjective, as in "a well-known author".
hints: Which words work together?
What do they describe?
The hyphen joins them.
items.explanation: The hyphen shows that well and known work together to describe the noun.

items.prompt: True or false: A hyphen is used to join two separate sentences.
hints: What does a hyphen connect?
Think of well-known.
Not whole sentences.
items.explanation: A hyphen joins words or parts of words. Sentences are joined by connectives or a semicolon.

items.prompt: True or false: A hyphen can avoid confusion, as in "re-cover the sofa", meaning cover it again.
hints: Compare re-cover and recover.
Do they mean the same?
The hyphen makes the meaning clear.
items.explanation: Without the hyphen, recover means to get better.

items.prompt: True or false: The phrase "a ten-year-old girl" is correctly hyphenated.
hints: Which word is the noun?
The words ten, year and old work together.
Hyphens join a describing phrase before a noun.
items.explanation: The hyphens join the words that together describe the noun girl.

items.prompt: True or false: The sentence "The girl is ten-years-old" is correctly hyphenated.
hints: Does the phrase come before a noun?
It follows the verb.
No hyphens are needed after the verb.
items.explanation: After the verb is, we write ten years old without hyphens.

items.prompt: True or false: A comma can change the meaning of a sentence, as in "Let's eat, Grandma" and "Let's eat Grandma".
hints: Compare the two versions.
Who is being spoken to?
The comma separates the name from the rest.
items.explanation: The comma shows that we are speaking to Grandma rather than eating her.
